trails.title: Public Radio Usage Log
trails.description: Next to this empty radio dock is a log that's been diligently updated with each use.

content.text:
Public radio. Five minutes per person per day. Listen to whatever you want, but leave an update in the log.

...

12:05 Restored the frequency to normal and listened to Swan Lake.

18:05 Tuned to a foreign station. Adjusted the frequency to avoid interference.

03:05 Attempt 39, still no reply from the cosmic friend. Answer me ... answer me ...

12:05 Restored the frequency to normal and listened to Swan Lake.

18:05 Tuned to a foreign station. Adjusted the frequency to avoid interference.

...

03:05 Attempt 42, observed an unusual aurora. Must be the cosmic friend, she's responding.

12:05 Restored the frequency to normal and listened to Swan Lake. Wishful thinking aside, remember to reset the settings.

18:05 Tuned to a foreign station. Adjusted the frequency to avoid interference.

...

03:05 Attempt 73, The terns' migration route is different from last year. Is she affecting the magnetic field?

12:08 Plesetsk is not going buy a second radio. Break it again, and we'll bury you in the snow.

18:05 Tuned to a foreign station. Adjusted the frequency to avoid interference.

...

03:05 Attempt 106, the magnetic anomaly has reached the edge of the polar circle. I so want to meet her.

12:00 Off to intercept a cosmic idealist in Mirny, break his bones, and reclaim the radio.

18:00 I hope his imaginary cosmic friend is real. As if.

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "Not long ago, Voyager 2 successfully reached Uranus, marking the first-ever exploration of this planet in human history. It conducted an examination of Uranus's ring system as planned ..."

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "After a temporary orbital adjustment caused by its earlier visit to Titan, Voyager 1 continues its journey towards the edge of the solar system ..."

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "Their future ..."
Plesetsk Office, Cosmodrome
The staticky but steady voice of the news cuts out.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We already know where they're going and what they're gonna do. Why are you wasting time on old news?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: As I recall, we've even got a photo from Voyager 1 taken in 1990. It's stored somewhere in the Laplace archives.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That's correct. They even have the development reports from Setun and the work done on meteor burst communication tech.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But none of the archives mention the whereabouts of the Golden Records, do they?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: So there is a chance we'll hear some new clue this time around, like "According to the sudden decrease in Voyager 1's mass, it's been speculated that the Golden Records were intercepted by an unknown entity ..."

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: "Intercepted," you make it sound like it was stolen by aliens, or space pirates!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: A space pirate? I doubt they would have any interest in some ordinary records.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Now why don't you get to the point? What's so urgent that you had to switch off the radio?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, I'm making a video. I didn't want the sound drowning out the recording.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Should be quiet enough now.
April 1986, Plesetsk Cosmodrome
Hissabeth, Laplace Researcher.
So, why was I mad enough to join this project? Call it a matter of personal interest.

Правда? 
"Really"?
Let me introduce myself in a little more detail, in case you're shocked when you get your first look at me.
Hallway, Cosmodrome

items.speaker: Snake I
items.text: Are we there yet? Drats! This is no way to travel! Let me just slither please.

items.speaker: Snake V
items.text: We don't have a choice. We're stuck with this most unfortunate mode of transportation.
Introducing two of the nine siblings of the Dubois family, always loudly at odds and proud of it.
Thanks to the cold weather, the others're still brumating, so they haven't yet tested my patience.
Footsteps grow nearer, prompting them to look around for their source.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Welcome. Let me walk you to your office.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Your ID card, please.

items.speaker: Snake I
items.text: Hiss.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Oh, my apologies!
My patience just ran out.
The snake twists its body away with agility, but not fast enough. It is forced to clamp its mouth shut.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Thank you for showing me the way.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Why don't we speed up a bit? This place feels as cold as a goddamn morgue. I can barely talk without shivering.
When we get to the office, I'll warn them not to scare our colleagues for the fourth time.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Of course. We'll ensure the heat is kept on 24/7 inside your office. Laplace never neglects the little details.
In truth, as a reptile enthusiast, she's just trying to hide the rudeness of her surprise at seeing the cute snakes.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Here we are. Go ahead and knock on the door. Ms. Pointer should be expecting you.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: By the way, since you mentioned the cold weather, do you need a thermostat for your lovely pets?

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: We try our best to meet all of our researchers' needs.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, we're all good. My coat works as a kind of thermo-regulated insulator. It should be fine.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Understood. And please note that the spaceport here is just a part of our local research collaboration. Laplace's official branch in Plesetsk is actually further north, right on the edge of the Arctic Circle.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: It has a strict security policy. So, you'll need to file an application before visiting. There's no guarantee it will be approved either.

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Welcome to the Plesetsk Cosmodrome.
Just a few steps out, the receptionist turns back, drawn by a faint sound.
The little golden-scaled snake flicks its tongue at her, and—was that a wink?

items.speaker: Receptionist
items.text: Goodbye, little hissie.
The researcher disappears down the hall, and cheerful voices ring out again.

items.speaker: Snake I
items.text: You know what, Two, I think the staff here are more accommodating than most types we meet.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Or, are you just being more of a jerk than usual?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Now stay out of trouble, and don't call me by my number again.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Just so you know, I'm perfectly willing to tie you up by the tails if I start hearing about any "missing lab rats."
The door swings open, preventing the escalation of their family feud.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I knew I heard someone talking behind the door. Glad my ears don't need tuning.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Please, come in. Are you the new researcher on this project?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You've got it. So, I take it you're one of my new colleagues?
Office, Cosmodrome
The new colleague's attitude seems cold to the touch.
But once she steps inside and takes in the whole setup, she realizes that details like that won't matter too much.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Two devices, two chairs, and two standard-issue desks.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Is it just the two of us?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I expected you to be more rigorous as a fellow Laplace researcher! According to official records, we have a third researcher on the team, an attache from the local government. In theory anyway, no one has ever seen or heard of them. It's just a name on the noticeboard.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: However, if you insist on ignoring our esteemed coworker—who I mention out of deep respect for our local partners—then correct, it's just the two of us.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: So, what do you think of our setup? It's not so bad. At least, we're in full control of our budget.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Although, I recommend setting those budget expectations low.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Cool, cool. Everything's more or less as I expected—an undervalued project in extraordinary times.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What kind of bizarre mind hatched up the idea of teleporting supplies directly into space?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Do you believe our goals are unrealistic?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Not at all. Only eclectic, let's say. And I've always been a fan of eclectic theories. They are often a stepping stone to true discovery.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I'm certain that the combination of arcanum and science will one day make up the core of our civilization. We're not there yet, but ...

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It's only a matter of time. Perhaps this project will be the next leap forward.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: So far, the teleport disk we've developed is functional but unstable. It's a one-way ticket capable of travel only within a short distance. But if we can improve its range and stability, I calculate its value to society to be potentially earth-shaking.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Looks like we'll make for quite a team.
She picks up the stack of files from the desk, clearing a small spot to lean against.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: But before that, we'll have to make sure our project isn't shut down before it can begin, which means we need to cook up something worthwhile to put in our report.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: To that end, I know you're an expert in aerospace materials. Are there any specific specimens you need? I'll do what I can to source them for you.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Oh, but be quick. Our resource applications must be submitted today. The evaluation process and all other little details mean it will take some time to arrive.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Let me see. Hmm, no, I don't have any particular needs for now. How do you feel about fish?
Even Pointer's keen analytical mind struggles to keep up with the rapid topic change.
She pauses a full three seconds before answering.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: They're fine, as are those pets you've got dangling in your hair.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Cool. Looks like I've come to exactly the right place. No nosy layabouts around to moan about my hobbies.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Speaking of those "pets," they're not really pets. I remember mentioning them in my profile. You didn't read it, hmm?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: "Whatever, so long as they can hold their own!" Then you threw the file into the trash. Am I right?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It wasn't quite so dramatic, but yes. I briefly scanned it for your field of expertise and experience. Nothing else mattered to me.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Still, you should get to know your new colleagues. I'm a Melusine. We have snakes for hair. So, they're not pets. They're my siblings.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Technically, you've got yourself a grand total of nine new coworkers. Surprise!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That is certainly new information. It's unfortunate that Laplace doesn't pay out their Sharpodonties by head.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Maybe I can convince them to go in for every two heads?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I wouldn't predict your chances to be high, but a larger food allowance seems appropriate, given your additional mouths to feed.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Mind requesting me a corner office? I need a lot of space for my fish tank. Pets and plants help me cool off.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Whatever you want, let's just finish the report as soon as possible. Then we can apply for additional office space—one room for each of us. Deal?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Deal.
Agreement reached. Pointer lifts her right hand.
A snake stretches forward to gently tap her palm with its head.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Nice working with you.
